title: Native ordinary open tensor constructions
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], schemes $X,Z$ in a common universe, and an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$. The actual varying-coefficient extension and pullback for the positive quotient rings, together with their fixed native adjunction and section-unit maps of [def-coef-native-open-tensor-evaluation-data], admit the ordinary/cochain data of [def-sf-open-tensor-cochain-data] on the ringed sequence sites. For every $n\in\mathbf N$, the actual finite functors $\mathrm{StrictTower.moduleJ}$ and $\mathrm{modulePullback}$ at the positive quotient stage $n+1$ admit the same ordinary/cochain data. These types are $\mathrm{SystemOpenCochains}(\ell,E,j)$ and $\mathrm{FiniteOpenCochains}(\ell,E,j,n)$, obtained by explicitly specializing that data definition to the displayed native functors. No derived calculus or derived tensor comparison is assumed or constructed.

proof.text: Identify the native open sites, coefficient sheaves, and exact module adjunctions with their localized-site presentations. Restriction of sheafification of tensor gives the natural ordinary restriction comparison and its specified pure-section formula. The ordinary direct image is the right adjoint of the native restriction.
Restriction preserves flat sheaves and flat-term K-flat complexes by the pullback preservation theorem, on both the sequence site and each finite site.

Use the unit transpose of the inverse restriction/tensor comparison as the inverse ordinary projection. The ringed-slice tensor formula and open-unit normalization prove it invertible; adjunction uniqueness proves ordinary naturality.

Totalize this natural comparison using preservation of coproducts. The signed differential and arbitrary chain-map naturality equations are the bidegree equations of the total-tensor theorem. Transport its summand formula through the exact site equivalences. Apply on the sequence site itself, retaining all horizontal quotient maps, and at every finite coefficient stage.
